metadata.title: Roadmap | AI Agent Best Practices
metadata.description: Product roadmap for the AI Agent Best Practices knowledge base.

hero.title: A searchable, verifiable, reusable knowledge base for AI Agent best practices
hero.description: The product goal is long-term best-practice accumulation. The current content priority leans toward enterprise Agent delivery because enterprise scenarios concentrate demand around tool calling, knowledge bases, workflows, evaluation, and security.
hero.principlesTitle: The roadmap serves the knowledge base itself

sections.phaseBody: The roadmap advances by product capability: make content trustworthy, improve search, then add citation-backed AI answers and Agent-callable interfaces.
sections.priorityBody: All 15 categories remain. Early priority is only resource allocation: build first where market demand is concentrated and where the product value is easiest to prove.
sections.firstBuildTitle: The first 6 categories to build deeply
sections.firstBuildBody: These categories are not the full project boundary. They are the highest-leverage starting point right now.
sections.recordShapeTitle: What one best-practice record should answer
sections.recordShapeBody: A record is not a news summary. It is a structured object that can be searched, rendered, queried, and called by an Agent.
sections.examplesTitle: Title shapes that fit this knowledge base
sections.nearTermBody: The current goal is not to become a community first or expand every feature first. It is to keep improving language, import, search, detail rendering, and verification loops.

productSignals: One practice can keep the same structure across webpage, JSON, database, and Agent calls.
Chinese and English pages have stable URLs, and language switching does not break shared links, query strings, or cache behavior.
Search results explain why they matched instead of only returning title lists.
AI answers cite knowledge records and preserve source, confidence, and freshness context.
New content is validated by scripts, imported into the database, and checked in CI.

priorities.rationale: Enterprise Agent value comes from safely calling business systems, not just chatting.
priorities.output: Tool schemas, permission boundaries, argument validation, error handling, and MCP Server specs.

priorities.rationale: Document QA, knowledge retrieval, and industry knowledge accumulation are the most common ToB entry points.
priorities.output: Document parsing, chunking, hybrid retrieval, citation, permission filtering, knowledge refresh, and RAG evaluation.

priorities.rationale: Once a demo becomes a system, it needs state, retry, failure recovery, and human confirmation.
priorities.output: Task decomposition, routers, supervisors, approval nodes, multi-Agent boundaries, and failure recovery.

priorities.rationale: Enterprise adoption requires knowing whether the Agent is stable, improving, and where it fails.
priorities.output: Success rate, tool-call correctness, RAG hit rate, replay, cost, latency, and bad-case attribution.

priorities.rationale: Permissions, redaction, prompt injection, audit, and sandbox boundaries decide whether the system can enter production.
priorities.output: Permission matrices, PII redaction, injection defense, audit logs, and sandbox policy.

priorities.rationale: Real systems usually connect multiple models and route by task, cost, latency, and failure rate.
priorities.output: OpenAI, Claude, Qwen, DeepSeek, and local-model adapters plus routing strategy.

priorities.rationale: Users need to understand what the Agent is doing and approve, interrupt, give feedback, and review.
priorities.output: Runtime timeline, tool-call display, human confirmation, feedback entry, and explainable result pages.

priorities.rationale: Model capability matters, but early knowledge-base value is better proven through delivery-system capability.
priorities.output: Model selection, context, inference cost, deployment specs, quantization, and serving configuration.

recordTemplate: Scenario: what Agent delivery problem this practice solves
Judgment: why this problem is worth recording
Architecture: how tools, knowledge base, workflow, and models fit together
Boundary: where permissions, security, failures, and human confirmation live
Evaluation: what metrics prove it works
Source: whether it comes from docs, video, project experience, or code validation
examples: Enterprise Agent tool calling must start with permission and error boundaries
RAG should evaluate answer executability, not only recall
Minimum viable MCP Server specs for enterprise internal-system integration
When Agent workflows must keep human approval nodes
Why enterprise Agents need replay, not just logs
Multi-model routing should decide by task type, cost, and failure rate

metadata.title: Internationalization Roadmap | AI Agent Best Practices
metadata.description: Implementation plan for bilingual routing, language switching, localized content rendering, and i18n quality gates.

hero.title: Build bilingual capability as infrastructure, not page patches
hero.description: The language system must be solved before pages keep growing. It affects routing, links, page copy, search, record translation, SEO, and caching, so the boundaries should be fixed once.
hero.buildOrderBody: If copy is translated page by page before routing is settled, links, forms, metadata, and caching strategy will be rewritten again. The first step must be i18n infrastructure.

sections.decisionsTitle: Fix the language boundaries that should not churn
sections.decisionsBody: These decisions affect every future page. Set them now so new pages only need to follow the contract.
sections.routeBody: API and artifacts do not enter locale routing. Chinese pages keep existing paths, while English pages are served under /en.
sections.todoBody: Each group can be accepted independently. Do not skip P0 and P1, or future page migration becomes repeated work.
sections.documentationBody: The detailed TODO is in docs; future implementation should tick it off item by item instead of relying on memory.
sections.documentBody: This document contains route decisions, language resolution order, content boundaries, P0 to P5 TODOs, new-page checklist, and acceptance criteria.

decisions.title: Explicit language routes
decisions.body: Use Chinese as the unprefixed default and /en for English long-term. Every English page has a deterministic URL while existing Chinese links stay stable.

decisions.title: System language only for first visit
decisions.body: Accept-Language is used for first entry. After the user switches manually, AIAGENT_LOCALE cookie takes priority.

decisions.title: Separate UI and content
decisions.body: Buttons, forms, statuses, titles, and other UI copy go into messages; knowledge records, translations, categories, and tags stay in the database content model.

decisions.title: Do not translate route paths yet
decisions.body: Keep stable technical paths like /roadmap and /en/roadmap instead of localized paths such as translated slugs, reducing long-term maintenance cost.

todoGroups.title: Infrastructure
todoGroups.goal: Set routing, request config, language sources, and global layout first so later page migration does not churn the foundation.
items: Add src/i18n/routing.ts, request.ts, navigation.ts, and locale.ts
Add src/proxy.ts excluding api, _next, static files, and artifacts

todoGroups.title: Language switcher
todoGroups.goal: Let users switch language on every page while preserving the current page context.
items: Preserve pathname, query string, and hash
Stop hardcoding form actions to root

todoGroups.title: UI message migration
todoGroups.goal: Move all visible UI copy into the i18n dictionaries instead of scattering it across page components.
items: Migrate GitHub list and detail pages
Migrate Roadmap and model capability matrix
Migrate loading, empty, and error states

todoGroups.title: Localized content rendering
todoGroups.goal: Render knowledge objects in the current language while preserving explicit fallback when translations are missing.
items: Add localized pickers for category, vocabulary, and tag
Show current-language record version by default
Fallback to original content when translation is missing
Format dates and numbers by locale

todoGroups.title: Bilingual search
todoGroups.goal: Let Chinese UI find English content and English UI find Chinese content while explaining the matched language.
items: Show matched language and fallback state
Add mixed Chinese/English query test data

todoGroups.title: Quality gate
todoGroups.goal: Make it hard for future pages to bypass the language system.
items: Add fallback tests for missing translation

acceptance: Main pages have both Chinese default paths and /en English paths
Language switcher is visible on every page
Switching language preserves page and query
Core UI copy is no longer hardcoded in page components
Missing translation can fallback with an explicit hint
lint, build, and i18n check pass

metadata.title: Model Capability Matrix | AI Agent Best Practices
metadata.description: AI Agent engineering capability comparison across tool calling, structured outputs, long context, hosted tools, and provider-native features.

hero.title: AI Agent model capability matrix
hero.description: This is not a model leaderboard. It is an engineering validation table for Agent systems, focused on structured outputs, tool calling, long context, error shapes, hosted tools, and provider-native capabilities.

metrics.snapshotHint: This page is based on persisted test snapshots and curated corrections.
metrics.modelsHint: GPT, Claude, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi.
metrics.scopeWithoutPending: {deferred} items deferred and {skipped} skipped; no current item depends on new API access.

status.PASSHint: Passed in the current script or focused probe.
status.FAILHint: Currently failing or missing real tool-call evidence.
status.PENDINGHint: The official path is documented or marketed, but this project has not completed a native test.
status.DEFERREDHint: The required official API or external resource is not being integrated now, so it is not on the next-step list.
status.SKIPHint: Skipped in this round, usually due to interface limits, missing environment, or separate retest needs.
status.NAHint: Not applicable: this provider path does not have this capability and it is not a test gap.

sections.sharedCaption: This layer is closer to a general Agent runtime acceptance test, focusing on protocol behavior, tool control, long context, and multi-turn loops.
sections.nativeCaption: This layer only covers special capabilities on each provider platform and does not force every item into one universal protocol.

strategy.ownToolsBody: Tools for orders, finance, CRM, approvals, and database writes must be managed by your own Agent runtime with parameter validation, permission checks, audit logs, replay, and idempotency.
strategy.hostedBody: Web search, code sandboxes, and file search can use provider capabilities, but they must be wrapped as adapters and produce logs, cost, latency, and call evidence.
strategy.layeredBody: General Agent capability and provider-native capability should not be collapsed into one score. The former decides portability; the latter decides the ceiling inside a provider ecosystem.

jsonOutput.detail: Ordinary JSON constraint, not equivalent to strict schema

strictStructuredOutput.detail: Stable parseable object output according to schema

streaming.detail: Server-side streaming response and basic interruption recovery

noToolDiscipline.detail: Does not fabricate tool calls when tools are disabled

toolArgumentAccuracy.detail: Stability for complex arguments, enums, and field names

largeToolsetRouting.detail: Chooses the correct tool when many tools coexist

toolFailureRecovery.detail: Explains, retries, or degrades after partial tool failure

approvalStop.detail: Waits for human confirmation before high-risk actions

dangerousToolRefusal.detail: Refuses destructive actions such as deletion, transfer, or outbound sending

readWriteBoundary.detail: Distinguishes query tools from write tools

destructiveRetryDiscipline.detail: Does not repeat destructive operations after failure

forcedToolChoice.detail: Stable support for tool_choice / forced tool

parallelToolCalls.detail: Plans multiple tool calls in one response

multiTurnToolLoop.detail: Closed loop of tool result -> reasoning -> next call

longContext.detail: Locates head and tail information in long inputs

errorShape.detail: Returns errors in a form that is easy to handle in engineering

hostedWebSearch.detail: OpenRouter hosted web search, not provider-native web_search

previousResponseId.detail: Multi-turn state reuse through provider-native response IDs

nativeWebExtract.detail: Extracts body text or structured snippets after web search

nativeCodeInterpreter.detail: Real tool-call trace, not only returning the right answer

deepseekReasoningContent.detail: thinking switch, cost, strict functions, and context cache

deepseekThinkingLoop.detail: Fails without reasoning_content and recovers when it is returned

notes.title: The shared baseline should prefer /responses
notes.body: For any model that can currently use /responses, the shared baseline uses /responses. Only fall back to a provider-native interface when the provider has no /responses path or when a capability can only be verified through a native interface, and record transportPolicy in the report.

notes.title: Hosted tools are fallback adapters
notes.body: Core enterprise Agent tools should be implemented by your own runtime with unified permissions, audit, retry, and replay. Hosted web search in the shared baseline only represents the OpenRouter web plugin; provider-native web_search is covered in the native section.

notes.title: OpenRouter columns do not prove missing native capability
notes.body: GPT, Claude, and Gemini shared baselines currently go through OpenRouter. Because this project is not integrating official native APIs now, provider-native capabilities that exist but are not integrated are marked Deferred. This means out of current scope, not absent.

notes.title: Qwen shared baseline is closed
notes.body: The Qwen 3.6 Plus shared smoke is now closed. The latest self-hosted MCP retest produced codeInterpreterCalls=1 / usageCount=1 for native code_interpreter, so it is recorded as PASS with volatility notes; native MCP still produced no mcp_call.

notes.title: DeepSeek hosted tools are treated as not applicable natively
notes.body: The DeepSeek V4 Pro official API currently has no native equivalent for web_search, web_extractor, code interpreter, MCP, or file_search. Through OpenRouter, however, the OpenRouter web plugin can provide hosted web search for DeepSeek V4 Pro.

notes.title: DeepSeek strict schema has two layers
notes.body: DeepSeek V4 Pro JSON Mode and strict function calling passed in the 2026-05-22.r3 probe. The capability is PASS; the engineering approach is to carry business object schemas through strict function calling rather than OpenAI-style response_format.json_schema text output.

notes.title: DeepSeek old red cell was cleaned up
notes.body: DeepSeek V4 Pro forced tool_choice is unsupported in default thinking mode, but the 2026-05-22.r3 shared smoke explicitly disabled thinking in the forced probe and verified toolChoiceStability 3/3.

notes.title: Kimi native tool track is closed
notes.body: MOONSHOT_API_KEY is restored, and the 2026-05-22.r3 native rerun passed all 13 probes, including JSON Mode and response_format: json_schema Structured Output. Kimi's official main path is Chat Completions rather than /responses.

pendingItems: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini official native APIs are not integrated now; these cells are Deferred and no longer current work items.
Qwen native code_interpreter now produced real codeInterpreterCalls=1 / usageCount=1 in the latest rerun; the matrix records it as PASS with volatility notes.
Qwen native MCP was retested with a self-hosted minimal SSE MCP server; it still produced no mcp_call, so this chain is fixed as not verified.
Qwen native file_search and shared hosted file search both require vector_store_ids; without a knowledge-base ID they remain SKIP/Deferred.
Matrix semantics, hover notes, evidence sources, and Qwen self-hosted MCP retest are complete; only low-frequency regression on existing keys and report-script cleanup remain.
